chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ali ibn Saeed, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the nabbash (grave digger/excavator). He said: If grave-digging is not a customary practice for him, he is not amputated (of the hand) but is given ta'zir (discretionary punishment).

key_terms.النَّبَّاشِ: Grave digger or excavator, specifically one who digs up graves to steal.
key_terms.وَيُعَزَّرْ: And he is given ta'zir (discretionary punishment).
key_terms.يُقْطَعْ: He is amputated (referring to the fixed punishment of cutting the hand for theft).

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a grave digger who steals if it is not his customary profession?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi' (AS) to clarify the distinction between *qat' al-yad* (fixed amputation) and *ta'zir* (discretionary punishment) for grave robbers. The key criterion is whether grave-digging is the individual's established profession or custom; if not, the stricter fixed penalty is waived in favor of judicial discretion. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that fixed punishments require strict adherence to specific conditions, preventing their application in cases of lesser habitual involvement.
